descriptionChirho: The fleshy parts of the mouth used for speaking; by metonymy, speech or verbal expression. Used of honoring God with lips (Matt 15:8 / Mark 7:6 quoting Isa 29:13), confessing with lips (Heb 13:15 'fruit of lips'), speech of foreign tongues (1 Cor 14:21), and deceptive speech (Rom 3:13 'poison of asps under their lips'). Spanish 'labios', Arabic 'شِفَاه', Korean '입술(들)', Swahili 'midomo', Hindi 'होंठों' all denote the anatomical feature or speech organ.

The edge or border of a body of water; a semantic extension from 'lip/edge' to a geographical boundary (Heb 11:12, descendants as numerous as the sand on the seashore). This mirrors the Hebrew idiom (שָׂפָה 'lip' also means 'shore/bank' in the OT). Spanish 'orilla', Arabic 'شَاطِئ', Korean '가장자리', Swahili 'ukingo', Hindi 'किनारे' all denote a water's edge or bank, clearly distinguishing this from the body-part sense.
